rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation.

3Mg(s) + N₂(g) → Mg₃N₂(s)

items.followUp: Explain any five types of molecules classified according to the number of atoms they contain.

rubric.why: Tests identification of molecules containing one atom.
rubric.description: Identifies a monatomic molecule and states that it contains one atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and its defining number of atoms.

rubric.why: Tests identification of molecules containing two atoms.
rubric.description: Identifies a diatomic molecule and states that it contains two atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and its defining number of atoms.

rubric.why: Tests identification of molecules containing three atoms.
rubric.description: Identifies a triatomic molecule and states that it contains three atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and its defining number of atoms.

rubric.why: Tests identification of molecules containing four atoms.
rubric.description: Identifies a tetratomic molecule and states that it contains four atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and its defining number of atoms.

rubric.why: Tests identification of molecules containing more than four atoms.
rubric.description: Identifies a polyatomic molecule and states that it contains more than four atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and its defining number of atoms.

modelAnswer: A monatomic molecule contains one atom, for example He.
A diatomic molecule contains two atoms, for example O₂.
A triatomic molecule contains three atoms, for example H₂O.
A tetratomic molecule contains four atoms, for example P₄.
A polyatomic molecule contains more than four atoms, for example S₈.

items.followUp: State four general properties of ionic compounds.

rubric.why: Tests the usual melting and boiling point behaviour of covalent compounds.
rubric.description: States that covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either or both properties.

rubric.why: Tests the electrical conductivity of covalent compounds.
rubric.description: States that covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conductivity property.

rubric.why: Tests solubility in non-polar or organic solvents.
rubric.description: States that covalent compounds are generally soluble in organic or non-polar solvents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct solubility property.

rubric.why: Tests the usual solubility of covalent compounds in water.
rubric.description: States that covalent compounds are generally insoluble or poorly soluble in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct solubility property.

modelAnswer: Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points because the forces between their molecules are weak.
They are generally poor conductors of electricity because they do not contain free ions or electrons.
They are generally soluble in organic or non-polar solvents.
They are generally insoluble or only slightly soluble in water.

items.followUp: State five conclusions drawn from Rutherford’s alpha-particle scattering experiment.

rubric.why: Tests the main observation that most alpha particles passed straight through the foil.
rubric.description: States that most alpha particles passed through the gold foil without deflection.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this observation.

rubric.why: Tests the observation that a small number of alpha particles changed direction.
rubric.description: States that a few alpha particles were deflected through small angles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this observation.

rubric.why: Tests the rare observation of alpha particles scattering backwards.
rubric.description: States that very few alpha particles were deflected backwards or rebounded.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this observation.

rubric.why: Tests the conclusion about the relative size of the nucleus.
rubric.description: Concludes that the atom has a very small nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the nucleus as very small compared with the atom.

rubric.why: Tests the conclusions about nuclear charge, concentration of mass, or the space inside an atom.
rubric.description: States that the nucleus is positively charged and dense, or that most of the atom is empty space.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one of these valid conclusions.

modelAnswer: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil without any deflection.
A few alpha particles were deflected through small angles.
Very few alpha particles were deflected backwards or rebounded.
The atom contains a very small, positively charged nucleus that contains most of its mass.
Most of the atom is empty space.

items.followUp: Define vapour pressure and explain three factors that affect it.

rubric.why: Tests the definition of vapour pressure at equilibrium.
rubric.description: Defines vapour pressure as the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equilibrium vapour pressure definition.

rubric.why: Tests the effect of temperature on vapour pressure.
rubric.description: States that vapour pressure increases as temperature increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct trend.

rubric.why: Tests the effect of the nature of the liquid and its intermolecular forces.
rubric.description: States that stronger intermolecular forces lower vapour pressure, or that a more volatile liquid has higher vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct relationship.

rubric.why: Tests the effect of adding a non-volatile dissolved substance.
rubric.description: States that a non-volatile solute or dissolved impurity lowers vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct effect.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by the vapour of a liquid when the vapour and liquid are in dynamic equilibrium in a closed container.
As temperature increases, vapour pressure increases because more liquid molecules escape into the vapour phase.
The nature of the liquid affects its vapour pressure: stronger intermolecular forces give a lower vapour pressure, while more volatile liquids have higher vapour pressure.
A non-volatile dissolved impurity lowers the vapour pressure of a liquid.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a free radical and a molecular ion, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Tests the defining feature of a free radical.
rubric.description: Defines a free radical as an atom or group of atoms with an unpaired electron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the unpaired-electron feature.

rubric.why: Tests the distinction between a neutral radical and a charged molecular ion.
rubric.description: Distinguishes a free radical as neutral from a molecular ion, which is a charged group of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the charge distinction.

modelAnswer: A free radical is an atom or group of atoms with an unpaired electron; it is generally electrically neutral, for example Cl•.
A molecular ion is a group of atoms carrying a net positive or negative charge, for example NH₄⁺ or SO₄²⁻.

items.followUp: Explain why air is a mixture while carbon dioxide is a compound.

rubric.why: Tests why a soft drink is classified as a mixture.
rubric.description: States that a soft drink contains substances physically mixed in variable proportions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the mixture and variable-composition idea.

rubric.why: Tests why water is classified as a compound.
rubric.description: States that hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed ratio in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the fixed chemical composition of water.

modelAnswer: A soft drink is a mixture because water, sugar, flavourings and dissolved carbon dioxide are physically mixed, and their proportions can vary.
Water is a compound because hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed 2:1 atom ratio.

items.followUp: Why are the d-block and f-block elements named according to their blocks?

rubric.why: Tests why s-block elements are classified together.
rubric.description: States that the differentiating or last electron enters an s-subshell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the s-subshell reason.

rubric.why: Tests why p-block elements are classified together.
rubric.description: States that the differentiating or last electron enters a p-subshell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the p-subshell reason.

modelAnswer: In s-block elements, the differentiating (last) electron enters an s-subshell of the outermost shell.
In p-block elements, the differentiating (last) electron enters a p-subshell of the outermost shell.
